title: Model substitution: recovery brief and customer action cards (draft)
body:
Purpose:
This is a working draft for: (A) a concise status-page / status-message we can push during a gradual recovery when we automatically switched serving models for a subset of requests, and (B) a short, stakeholder-friendly post-incident summary and action card for affected customers.

Context summary (short):
On 2026-06-14 02:10 UTC Redwood’s routing layer automatically substituted a smaller, compatible model variant for a portion of live traffic in EU and US-west regions to preserve availability after an upstream kernel regression reduced capacity on several GPU pools. The substitution preserved availability but led to an increased rate of short-form hallucinations and truncated structured outputs for ~3.5% of tenant requests for approx 4 hours.

What to publish on status page (one-line and expanded):
- One-line (status page headline): Partial degradation: temporary model substitution active in EU + US-west; most requests unaffected; mitigation in progress.
- Expanded (status page details): Between 02:10 and 06:30 UTC we automatically routed some requests to a smaller model variant to keep inference endpoints online while affected nodes were drained. This resulted in a higher-than-normal rate of truncated structured responses and short factual errors for a small percentage of requests. We have completed validation and rolled back routing to primary variants in all regions. Customers with strict quality SLAs may have seen degraded responses between 02:10—06:30 UTC.

Customer-facing cause summary (plain language):
- Root cause (brief): A GPU driver/kernel mismatch caused reduced capacity on our primary serving pools. To avoid a total outage we activated our model-substitution policy which routes traffic to an available but lower-capacity model variant. That policy behaved as designed for availability but had quality tradeoffs for a subset of workloads.
- What we changed: We fixed the driver mismatch on affected hosts, resumed full-capacity pools, and reverted the model-substitution routing. We validated a sample of customer requests and saw quality return to baseline.

Impact (customer-facing):
- Who: ~3.5% of requests for customers served from EU and US-west regions during the window.
- What: Higher rate of truncated structured outputs and short factual inaccuracies in outputs for certain prompts (not a data leak; no customer data was exfiltrated).
- Severity: Low-to-moderate customer impact for applications that rely on deterministic structured outputs (e.g., JSON tool-calling, parsable summaries). Most conversational and free-text generation customers saw negligible effect.

Suggested status message snippets (for email or dashboard):
- Short (for in-app banner): We experienced a temporary model substitution in certain regions that may have slightly reduced answer quality for some requests. Full service has been restored.
- Medium (for customer email): On 14 Jun 2026 we automatically routed some traffic to a lower-capacity model variant to maintain availability after degraded GPU pool capacity. This prevented service disruptions but caused a small percentage of responses to be truncated or to contain brief inaccuracies. The issue has been fixed and we reverted routing. We are offering a verification package if you need replay evidence.
- Long (customer postmortem summary): See the timeline and technical notes below. We include suggested actions and a replay/evidence kit to help customers verify any affected requests.

Customer action card (what customers can/do):
- If you observed degraded outputs and require re-processing: Contact CS with tenant ID + approximate time window and we will (a) check replay logs and (b) offer a free re-run of those requests on the baseline model (subject to reasonable use).
- If you rely on strictly structured outputs: Consider adding lightweight result validation or schema checks in pre-prod to cancel or re-submit low-quality outputs. We will provide a sample schema-validation snippet and a short checklist.
- If you want telemetry: We can provide a CSV of request ids + timestamps for affected windows (consent required).

Timeline (UTC, concise):
- 2026-06-14 01:58 — Degraded host capacity detected in EU-west GPU pool; automated capacity alarms fired.
- 2026-06-14 02:10 — Model-substitution routing triggered automatically per policy to maintain availability.
- 2026-06-14 02:35 — First customer reports of truncated structured outputs (internal ticket JIRA-INC-3842).
- 2026-06-14 03:20 — Infra team identified driver/kernel mismatch candidate; mitigation plan initiated.
- 2026-06-14 05:45 — Patches deployed and affected nodes drained back into pool.
- 2026-06-14 06:10 — Routing reverted to primary model variants in EU and US-west.
- 2026-06-14 06:30 — Post-deployment validation completed; quality metrics returned to baseline.

Technical notes (for customers wanting more detail):
- The substitution targeted a quantized model family with identical API compatibility but fewer parameters and shorter max-context handling. It maintained token-level streaming behavior but had a higher chance of early EOS for certain structured output prompts.
- No private keys, PII or customer data left Redwood’s control; this was an availability/quality tradeoff only.
- We are adding a pre-route quality-sampling check to detect early signs of model-variant regressions in the future.

Customer evidence & replay kit (offering):
- If a customer requests validation we will provide: (1) a CSV of candidate request IDs and timestamps; (2) a short audit log showing which model variant served each request; (3) an option to re-run requests against the baseline model and produce a before/after diff.

Internal follow-ups (owner assignments):
- Infra: complete host driver audit and add scheduled driver compatibility checks — owner: Omar Haddad — due 2026-07-01.
- Serving runtime: add an integration test that simulates the quantized variant’s early-EOS behaviour on representative structured prompts — owner: Ravi Menon — due 2026-06-30.
- CS: prepare templated customer outreach and manage all replay requests — owner: Claire Wu — ongoing until customer backlog is cleared.

Open items / questions (notes to self):
- Do we want to offer automatic credits for tenants that requested >1000 replays? (cost review needed).
- Confirm which customers opted into debug logging during the window; coordinate privacy check before sharing IDs.
- Decide whether to publish the full technical postmortem publicly or keep a redacted customer-facing summary.

Suggested FAQ for customer portal:
Q: Will my data be shared?
A: No. We will only share request IDs and replay evidence with your explicit consent. No data was exfiltrated.

Q: Why did you substitute models instead of pausing service?
A: We prioritized availability for live applications. Substitution lets apps stay online while we remediate hardware-level issues; we accept quality tradeoffs as a known risk and provide replay/remediation options.

Q: How can I avoid exposure in future events?
A: Options: pin model version to dedicated pools (Dedicated customers), add stricter schema validation and a thin QA layer for structured responses, or whitelist-only critical routes to skip substitution (feature request/enterprise config).

Draft dispatch plan (who sends what):
- 06:45 UTC (ops): push status page Expanded notice + in-app banner (short snippet).
- 08:00 UTC (CS): targeted emails to top-10 affected tenants with replay offer and contact.
- 12:00 UTC (PM/Infra): internal postmortem posting to confluence + public summary draft for marketing review.

Notes on tone and escalation: keep the tone transparent, prioritize actionable remediation items, avoid technical jargon for customers unless they request it.

---- end of draft ----

Revision history:
- 2026-06-15: initial draft (Nina Shah)
- 2026-06-16: added timeline + technical notes (Ravi)
- 2026-06-18: updated recovery validation language and replay offer (Claire)
